# About this document {#sec-about .unnumbered}

Apptainer runs containers on HPC clusters and other shared Linux machines. It
runs them as the user who starts them, without root rights and without a
daemon, which is why clusters allow it. It was called Singularity until 2021;
SingularityCE continues Singularity separately, with mostly the same commands.
[](index.qmd) says when to use Apptainer and states the rules that hold for
every image; this document adds what is specific to Apptainer. Its rules use
the [normative language](../../principles/design.qmd#sec-normative) of
*Design Principles*.

Checked against Apptainer 1.5.4.


# At a glance {#sec-at-a-glance .unnumbered}

Every rule of this document in one line. The number and the title link to the
rule.

::: {.glance}
| No. | Rule | In one line |
|-----|------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------|
| [-@sec-host] | [](#sec-host) | Run steps with `--containall`, so that neither the environment nor the home directory of the host reaches the container. |
| [-@sec-binds] | [](#sec-binds) | Bind only the paths a step uses, and its inputs read-only. |
| [-@sec-sandbox] | [](#sec-sandbox) | Try things out in a sandbox, but build every image you use from its definition file. |
| [-@sec-test] | [](#sec-test) | Give every definition file a `%test` section that checks that the image is complete. |
| [-@sec-cache] | [](#sec-cache) | Point the cache and the temporary files of Apptainer away from the home directory. |
:::


# Rules {#sec-rules}


## Leave the host at the door {#sec-host}

Every step of a workflow should run with `--containall`, or with both
`--cleanenv` and `--no-home`, so that nothing of the host reaches the container
that the step does not declare. By default, Apptainer shares much of the host
with the container: every environment variable, the home directory, the current
directory, and `/tmp`. A step then depends not only on its image but also on
who runs it.

Two leaks are common, and each option stops only one of them. Python puts the
packages that the user installed with `pip install --user` into the home
directory and loads them before those of the image, and only `--no-home` keeps
them out. A `PYTHONPATH` or an `R_LIBS_USER` set on the host does the same, and
only `--cleanenv` keeps it out. Either way, the step computes with versions
that no lock file records, on one account and not on another: an undeclared
input ([](../../principles/design.qmd#sec-declared-inputs)) that defeats the
pinning of the image ([](../../principles/design.qmd#sec-pin)).

`--containall` implies both, and isolates processes as well; inside, the home
directory is empty and the current directory is not bound. Pass what a step
needs explicitly: data with `--bind` (@sec-binds), and variables with
`--env NAME=value` or `--env-file`. Interactive work may keep the defaults.


## Bind what a step needs, read-only what it reads {#sec-binds}

A step should bind only the directories it reads and writes, and its inputs
read-only, with `--bind source:destination:ro`. A step that sees only its
declared inputs fails loudly when it reaches for anything else, instead of
reading a file that nobody declared
([](../../principles/design.qmd#sec-declared-inputs)), and an input bound
read-only cannot be changed by mistake
([](../../principles/design.qmd#sec-mutation)).

Bind to fixed paths inside the container, such as `/data` and `/results`, not
to the paths of the host: the commands inside the container are then the same
on every machine, and only the binds change.


## Develop in a sandbox, release from the definition file {#sec-sandbox}

Every image that computes results should be built from its definition file.
A sandbox, an image as a writable directory made with
`apptainer build --sandbox`, is the place to find out what an image needs:
install and try things in it with `apptainer shell --writable`, then write each
step that worked into the definition file. An image converted from a sandbox
that was changed by hand has no recipe
([](../../principles/design.qmd#sec-recipe)): `apptainer inspect --deffile`
then shows only `bootstrap: localimage`, and nobody can rebuild, fix, or
update it.


## Test the image where it is built {#sec-test}

Every definition file should have a `%test` section that starts the main
programs of the image, for example by importing the packages of the analysis
and printing the version of each tool. Apptainer runs it at the end of every
build and fails the build if it fails, so an incomplete image is never
written; `apptainer test` runs it again on another machine. Its oracle is
"[it runs](../../principles/test-types.qmd#sec-it-runs)": it shows that the
image is complete, not that its results are right, which is the job of the
tests of the code and of the workflow
([](../../principles/design.qmd#sec-end-to-end)).


## Keep the cache off your home directory {#sec-cache}

On a cluster, set `APPTAINER_CACHEDIR` and `APPTAINER_TMPDIR` to a scratch or
project directory, for example in `~/.bashrc`. Apptainer keeps every image it
pulls in a cache, `~/.apptainer/cache` by default, and unpacks images for a
build in `/tmp`. Both grow by gigabytes, while the home directories and `/tmp`
of clusters are small, and a full quota makes later jobs fail with errors far
from the cause. `apptainer cache list` shows the cache, and
`apptainer cache clean` empties it.


# How Apptainer works {#sec-concepts}

An *image* is a single file in the Singularity Image Format (SIF), such as
`analysis.sif`: a compressed, read-only file system that holds the operating
system files, the libraries, and the programs, with metadata such as the
definition file it was built from and its labels. Copying the file copies the
whole environment, and its checksum identifies it. A *container* is a program
running in an image; it ends when the program ends.

Apptainer builds an image from a definition file (@sec-definition-file), or
converts one from a registry such as Docker Hub, squashing its layers into one
file. A *sandbox* is an image as a writable directory, for development
(@sec-sandbox).

Inside the container, the user is the same as outside, with the same rights: a
container cannot do anything its user cannot. By default, Apptainer binds the
home directory, the current directory, and `/tmp` of the host, passes every
environment variable, and shares the network, so that a container behaves much
like a program on the host (@sec-host). The image itself is read-only: a
program that writes into it fails and has to write into a bound directory
instead.


# Commands {#sec-commands}

| Command | Does |
|------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------|
| `apptainer pull out.sif docker://image@sha256:…` | Downloads an image from a registry and converts it into a SIF file |
| `apptainer build out.sif recipe.def` | Builds an image from a definition file; add `--fakeroot` if the build needs root rights |
| `apptainer exec image.sif command …` | Runs a command in the image |
| `apptainer run image.sif …` | Runs the `%runscript` of the image with the arguments |
| `apptainer shell image.sif` | Opens an interactive shell in the image |
| `apptainer test image.sif` | Runs the `%test` section of the image |
| `apptainer inspect --deffile image.sif` | Shows the definition file the image was built from; `--labels` shows its labels |
| `apptainer instance start image.sif name` | Runs the image in the background as a service; `instance list` and `instance stop name` |
| `apptainer cache list`, `apptainer cache clean` | Shows and empties the cache |

The options of `exec`, `run`, and `shell`:

| Option | Does |
|------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------|
| `--bind src:dest:ro` | Binds the host path `src` to `dest` in the container; `ro` read-only, `rw` the default; several separated by commas |
| `--containall` | Isolates the file systems, the environment, and the processes; binds neither the home nor the current directory |
| `--cleanenv` | Passes no environment variables of the host |
| `--no-home` | Does not bind the home directory |
| `--env NAME=value`, `--env-file file` | Passes the given environment variables, also with `--cleanenv` |
| `--pwd dir` | Starts in the directory `dir` inside the container |
| `--nv`, `--rocm` | Makes the GPUs of NVIDIA or AMD available (@sec-cluster) |
| `--writable-tmpfs` | Lets programs write into the image, in memory, until the container ends |

A typical step of a workflow, isolated from the host, with its input read-only:

```bash
apptainer exec --containall \
    --bind /scratch/project/data:/data:ro \
    --bind /scratch/project/results:/results \
    --pwd /results --env OMP_NUM_THREADS=8 \
    analysis.sif python /opt/analysis/run.py --input /data/samples.csv
```


# A definition file {#sec-definition-file}

A definition file, such as `analysis.def`, is the recipe of an image. Build it
with `apptainer build analysis.sif analysis.def` in the directory that holds
the files it copies.

```default
Bootstrap: docker
From: python:3.12-slim@sha256:<digest>

%files
    requirements.txt /opt/requirements.txt
    src /opt/analysis

%post
    pip install --no-cache-dir -r /opt/requirements.txt

%environment
    export LC_ALL=C.UTF-8
    export PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1

%runscript
    exec python /opt/analysis/run.py "$@"

%test
    python -c "import numpy; print('numpy', numpy.__version__)"
    python -c "import pandas; print('pandas', pandas.__version__)"

%labels
    org.opencontainers.image.source https://github.com/lab/analysis
    org.opencontainers.image.version 1.2.0
```

- **`Bootstrap` and `From`** name the base image, here one from Docker Hub,
  pinned by its digest ([](index.qmd#sec-pin)). The registry shows the digest,
  and so does `skopeo inspect docker://python:3.12-slim`.
- **`%files`** copies files and directories from the host into the image,
  before `%post` runs.
- **`%post`** runs once, during the build, as root inside the image: install
  the software here, with exact versions, such as from a `requirements.txt`
  that pins every package with `==`.
- **`%environment`** sets environment variables whenever the image runs.
  `PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1` keeps the packages of the user's home directory out even
  when the home directory is bound (@sec-host).
- **`%runscript`** is what `apptainer run` does.
- **`%test`** checks the image at the end of the build (@sec-test).
- **`%labels`** stores metadata, which `apptainer inspect --labels` shows.


# On a cluster {#sec-cluster}

**Slurm.** A job runs Apptainer like any other program, and Slurm grants the
resources:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=8
#SBATCH --mem=16G
#SBATCH --time=02:00:00

srun apptainer exec --containall \
    --bind "$SCRATCH/data:/data:ro" --bind "$SCRATCH/results:/results" \
    --env OMP_NUM_THREADS="$SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK" \
    analysis.sif python /opt/analysis/run.py --input /data/samples.csv
```

Workflow managers, such as Nextflow and Snakemake, start each step in its
image themselves; pass the options of @sec-host through their settings for
extra options of Apptainer.

**GPUs.** `--nv` makes the NVIDIA GPUs that the job was granted available in
the container, together with the driver of the host; the CUDA version in the
image must be one that this driver supports. `--rocm` does the same for AMD.

**MPI.** In the usual hybrid model, the MPI of the host starts the processes,
with `srun` or `mpirun`, and each runs in the container; the MPI library in the
image must be compatible with that of the host, which in practice means the
same implementation and a compatible version. The documentation of the cluster
says which MPI to put into the image.

**Building.** Many clusters let users build images only with `--fakeroot`, or
not at all. Build where you can, on a Linux machine, in a virtual machine on
macOS or Windows, or in continuous integration, and copy the SIF file to the
cluster, or push the image to a registry and pull it there. Build for the
processor architecture of the cluster: an image built on an ARM machine, such
as a Mac with Apple silicon, does not run on an x86 cluster.
